summary: Keiji Kokubu was a philosopher who studied at Ryukoku University and under Tokuryu Yamauchi. He held posts at Ryukoku University, Nanzan University, and Ritsumeikan University.

Keiji Nishitani worked in philosophy and religious studies, studying under Kitarō Nishida and Hajime Tanabe at Kyoto University, and Martin Heidegger at the University of Freiburg. He taught at Otani University (~1928–1935, ~1965–1971) and Kyoto University (1935–1964).

Keiki Yabuki was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied at Tohoku Fukushi, Taisho, and Tokyo universities. He taught at Shukyo University (~1913–1926), the University of Tokyo (~1924–1939), and Taisho University (~1926–1939).
Keikyo Nakamikado works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Nakamikado held research positions at Bukkyo University (attested 2003) and the Chion-in Institute of Jodo Sect Studies (attested 2015).

Keir Strickland specializes in Indology, history, and archaeology. He completed a PhD at Durham University under Robin Coningham (~2007–2011) and held posts at the University of the Highlands and Islands (2012–2016) and La Trobe University (2016).
Keishi Renja is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed doctoral coursework at Taisho University (attested 2013), where Renja also served as a research student.

Keishin Okamura was a Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral studies at Kyoto University. Okamura held academic posts at Koyasan University (1959–1973, 2005–2009) and served as a professor at Kochi University until 1995.

Keisho Tsukamoto was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctorate from Tohoku University. He held positions at Rissho University (~1959–1978), Tohoku University (~1978–1992), and served as president of Hosen Gakuen College (~1994–2000).

Keisuke Fujii is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who earned his doctorate from the University of Tokyo. He held positions at the University of Tokyo from 1982 to 2018 and at Tokyo University of the Arts.

Keith Dowman is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and under Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje, Kangyur Rinpoche, and Dilgo Khyentse, among other teachers. He held a post at Sonoma State University in 1973.

Keiya Noguchi is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who completed doctoral studies at Kyoto University. He held posts at Shuchiin University (attested 1995–2005) and Taisho University (attested 1995–2017).

Keizaburo Mizuno studied at the University of Tokyo, working in Japanology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He worked at the Tokyo National Museum (1958–1968), Tokyo University of the Arts (emeritus 1996, ~2000), and directed the Niigata Prefectural Museum of Modern Art.
Keizo Kojima studied at Hitotsubashi University (~1937–1941) and under Tokuryu Yamauchi, working in philosophy. Kojima held an academic post at Sophia University.

Kelsang Gyatso was a Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy scholar who studied at Sera, Jampa Ling, and Tashi Lhunpo monasteries and under Trijang Rinpoche. He taught at the Manjushri Kadampa Meditation Centre from 1977 and founded the New Kadampa Tradition.

Kelsey Alise Seymour specializes in Sinology and Buddhist studies, earning a PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under Victor H. Mair (attested 2018). Seymour was a visiting predoctoral fellow at the Max Planck Institute for the History of Science (2017–2018).
Kemo Jin worked in Indology, Sinology, and linguistics. Jin held posts at Visva-Bharati University (1941–1945) and served as Professor of Sanskrit at Peking University beginning in 1948.

Ken McLeod is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at the University of British Columbia and under Kalu Rinpoche and Dezhung Rinpoche. He served as resident teacher at Kagyu Dongak Chuling (~1985–1990) and founded Unfettered Mind.
Kendall Marchman is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied under Mario Poceski and earned a PhD from the University of Florida in 2015.

Kengo Harimoto works in Indology and philosophy, earning a PhD from the University of Pennsylvania under Wilhelm Halbfass. He has held positions at Temple, Hamburg, Leiden, Mahidol, and Naples "L'Orientale" universities.
Kenji Ishii is a religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1973–1982). He held an academic post at Kokugakuin University from approximately 1988 to 2020.
